Accessibility Expertise with a Practical, Hands-On Approach

Kaffeinated Kodemonkey is a small, specialized web accessibility business founded by Heather Welsh. We combine web development experience with dedicated accessibility testing to help organizations identify barriers, understand their impact, and make informed improvements.

As a DHS Certified Trusted Tester, Heather brings a structured approach to manual accessibility evaluation, supported by automated scanning and practical technical knowledge. Our work focuses on more than identifying potential issues—we help clients understand evaluation findings, prioritize remediation, and document their accessibility efforts.

We work with public agencies, educational institutions, and businesses that need experienced accessibility support, whether they are evaluating an existing website, improving development practices, or building accessibility into a new digital project.

Our approach is straightforward: practical expertise, clear reporting, and support tailored to your organization's needs.

Learn About Our Services

Web Accessibility Services

Kaffeinated Kodemonkey helps organizations evaluate, improve, and maintain digital accessibility. Led by a DHS Certified Trusted Tester, our services include automated scanning, manual evaluation, reporting, and accessibility-first development, as appropriate to each project's scope. We support organizations working toward applicable WCAG 2.1/2.2 and Section 508 requirements, with a practical focus on identifying barriers and helping teams address them.

WCAG Accessibility Audit & POCC

Get a scoped WCAG accessibility audit using manual DHS Trusted Tester testing and automated scans powered by WAVE. Findings appear in a WCAG Evaluation Audit Report (WEAR), delivered with POCC documentation.

Evaluation Options:

  • POCC Documentation: A full WCAG accessibility audit, WEAR report, and supporting Proof of Compliance Certificate documentation.
  • VPAT / ACR Option: Baseline automated scanning and VPAT/ACR preparation for organizations that need accessibility conformance reporting. Manual DHS Trusted Tester evaluation is not included.
Explore Evaluations

Accessibility Monitoring

Automated monitoring scans agreed website pages for detectable accessibility issues as content and code change. Scan coverage and frequency are established during scoping; automated findings may need manual verification.

Monitoring Options:

  • Ongoing Scanning: Scan configured pages for detectable issues as content and code change.
  • Multi-Site Monitoring: Support multiple websites, subject to the agreed plan and configured coverage.
  • Scheduled Audits: Quarterly manual evaluations and WEAR reports complement ongoing automated monitoring.
Explore Monitoring

Accessibility-First Web Development

Plan accessibility into a new website or redesign. We work with organizations and their teams on accessible design and development, with scope and testing defined for each project.

Development Options:

  • Accessible Foundations: Thoughtful page structure, navigation, forms, and reusable components.
  • Purpose-Fit Technology: Platforms and tools selected around project requirements.
  • CMS Options: Content management options considered around your team's publishing needs.
  • Accessibility in Practice: Development informed by accessibility standards, testing, and remediation experience.

Automated Scanning Is a Starting Point. Manual Testing Goes Further

Automated accessibility tools can identify many potential issues across a website, helping teams establish a baseline and prioritize areas for review. However, automated results alone cannot determine whether every aspect of a website is accessible.

At Kaffeinated Kodemonkey, we combine automated accessibility scanning with manual testing using the DHS Trusted Tester process. This approach helps us investigate potential barriers, evaluate applicable accessibility requirements, and document findings that teams can use to plan remediation.

Our evaluation process includes:

  • Automated baseline scanning: Identify potential issues, recurring patterns, and pages or features that need closer attention.
  • Structured manual testing: Evaluate applicable accessibility requirements using the DHS Trusted Tester process.
  • Documented findings: Record results in a WCAG report with suggested remediation steps to help organizations understand what needs attention.

The result is a more useful picture of your website's accessibility than an automated scan alone can provide.

Frequently Asked Questions About Web Accessibility

A website accessibility evaluation examines a website for barriers that may prevent people with disabilities from accessing or using its content and functionality. Kaffeinated Kodemonkey combines automated scanning with manual testing using the DHS Trusted Tester process to document findings and recommend improvements.

The Proof of Compliance Certificate (POCC) is part of Kaffeinated Kodemonkey's accessibility evaluation and documentation package. The package includes an Accessibility Statement, a WCAG report, and suggested remediations. It documents the evaluation performed and its findings; it is not a government-issued certification or a guarantee of legal compliance.

Automated scanning can identify many potential accessibility issues efficiently, but it cannot reliably evaluate every accessibility requirement. Manual testing allows an evaluator to examine applicable requirements and interactions more closely. Combining both approaches provides more useful findings than relying on automated results alone.

Yes. Organizations that need an Accessibility Conformance Report can request a separate evaluation and reporting option using the applicable Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT). The appropriate reporting approach depends on the product or service being evaluated and the organization's requirements.

Yes. Kaffeinated Kodemonkey supports public agencies, educational institutions, and businesses with accessibility evaluations, documentation, monitoring, and accessibility-first web development. Services can be discussed in the context of your organization's requirements and existing digital environment.

Yes. We can provide remediation guidance, accessibility consulting, monitoring, and development support. The appropriate next step depends on your findings, your team's capabilities, and whether you need help correcting issues or monitoring changes over time.

No single scan or evaluation can guarantee that a website will remain accessible or satisfy every legal obligation. An evaluation documents the scope of testing and the findings identified during that process. Ongoing maintenance, content changes, and follow-up testing remain important parts of accessibility management.
